introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
When electromagnetic radiation of sufficiently high frequency falls on a clean metal surface, electrons are emitted from it. Even the most energetic electron is prevented from leaving the metal surface when a stopping potential, $V$ is applied to the metal. The frequency of the incident radiation and the stopping potential of the metal are related by the equation

$$hf - hf_0 - eV = 0$$

where $e$ is electronic charge, $h$ and $f_0$ are constants.

In one such experiment to verify the relationship between the frequency of incident radiation and the stopping potential of a clean zinc plate, the following data was obtained.

| $V$ / V | $f$ / $\times10^{14}$ Hz |
|---|---|
| 1.30 | 6.0 |
| 2.95 | 10.0 |
| 4.17 | 14.0 |
| 6.25 | 19.0 |
| 8.33 | 24.0 |
| 10.40 | 30.0 |
| 12.45 | 35.0 |
| 14.53 | 41.0 |
incertitudes: Question 7 : marques imprimées 9 + 8 + 3 = 20, conformes au « Total = 20 marks ». Le graphe (a) est à tracer par le candidat ; le corrigé donne les grandeurs portées sur chaque axe, le tableau, les échelles, la droite et les lectures, sans produire de figure de corrigé.

Question 7 : ajustement par moindres carrés des huit points : V = 0,380 f - 0,961 (f en 10^14 Hz, V en volts, coefficient de corrélation 0,9997), d'où h = e x pente = 6,08 x 10^-34 J s (avec e = 1,60 x 10^-19 C), f0 = 2,53 x 10^14 Hz et un travail d'extraction de 0,96 eV (1,54 x 10^-19 J). Les valeurs lues sur un graphe à la main varient légèrement (h entre 6,0 et 6,2 x 10^-34 J s).

Question 7 : les données imprimées ne reproduisent pas les valeurs du zinc réel (travail d'extraction d'environ 4,3 eV, f0 d'environ 1,0 x 10^15 Hz) ; le corrigé exploite les données telles qu'imprimées, sans les corriger.

questions.enonce_markdown: Plot a suitable graph from which $h$ and $f_0$ can be calculated.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Choice of graph.** Rearrange the equation to the form $y = mx + c$:
$$hf - hf_0 - eV = 0\quad\Rightarrow\quad V = \frac{h}{e}\,f - \frac{h}{e}\,f_0.$$
So plot **the stopping potential $V$ (vertical axis) against the frequency $f$ (horizontal axis)**. The graph is a straight line with

- gradient $= \dfrac{h}{e}$;
- intercept on the $f$-axis ($V = 0$): $f = f_0$;
- intercept on the $V$-axis: $-\dfrac{hf_0}{e}$.

**Table of points to plot:**

| $f$ / $\times10^{14}$ Hz | 6.0 | 10.0 | 14.0 | 19.0 | 24.0 | 30.0 | 35.0 | 41.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $V$ / V | 1.30 | 2.95 | 4.17 | 6.25 | 8.33 | 10.40 | 12.45 | 14.53 |

**How to draw it.**

- Label the axes with the quantity and the unit ($V$ / V and $f$ / $10^{14}$ Hz).
- Choose scales that use more than half of the graph paper in each direction, for example $2\ \mathrm{cm}$ for $5\times10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$ on the $f$-axis starting at $0$ and $2\ \mathrm{cm}$ for $2\ \mathrm{V}$ on the $V$-axis. Extend the $f$-axis down to $0$ and the $V$-axis to about $-1.5\ \mathrm{V}$ so that the intercepts can be read.
- Plot the eight points accurately (to within half a small square) and draw one straight line of best fit with the points evenly scattered on both sides of it. The points lie very close to a straight line (the largest deviation is about $0.2\ \mathrm{V}$), which verifies the relationship.
- Extend the line back until it cuts the $f$-axis.

The best-fit line is $V = 0.380\,f - 0.961$ (with $f$ in units of $10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$).

**Gradient** (large triangle taken on the line, from $f = 5.0\times10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz},\ V = 0.94\ \mathrm{V}$ to $f = 40.0\times10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz},\ V = 14.25\ \mathrm{V}$):
$$\text{gradient} = \frac{14.25 - 0.94}{(40.0 - 5.0)\times10^{14}} = \frac{13.31}{35.0\times10^{14}} = 3.80\times10^{-15}\ \mathrm{V\,s}.$$

**Planck constant.** The gradient is $h/e$, so with $e = 1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$
$$h = e\times\text{gradient} = 1.60\times10^{-19}\times3.80\times10^{-15} = 6.08\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}.$$

**Threshold frequency.** The line cuts the $f$-axis (where $V = 0$) at
$$f_0 = \frac{0.961}{0.380}\times10^{14} = 2.53\times10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}.$$
(Check from the $V$-intercept: $-\dfrac{hf_0}{e} = -0.96\ \mathrm{V}$, giving the same $f_0$.)

**$h \approx 6.1\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$ and $f_0 \approx 2.5\times10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$** (values read from a hand-drawn graph may differ slightly).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is the physical significance of $f_0$?

(ii) Calculate the work function of zinc.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** $f_0$ is the **threshold frequency**: the minimum frequency of the incident radiation that can eject electrons from the metal surface. For $f < f_0$ no electrons are emitted, however intense the radiation; at $f = f_0$ the emitted electrons have zero kinetic energy (so $V = 0$).

**(ii)** The work function $\phi$ is the minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the surface:
$$\phi = hf_0 = 6.08\times10^{-34}\times2.53\times10^{14} = 1.54\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}\ \left(= \frac{1.54\times10^{-19}}{1.60\times10^{-19}} = 0.96\ \mathrm{eV}\right).$$
(Equivalently $\phi = e\times|V\text{-intercept}| = 0.96\ \mathrm{eV}$.)

**Work function of zinc from these data $\approx 1.5\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}\ (0.96\ \mathrm{eV})$.** (The tabulated value for zinc is about $4.3\ \mathrm{eV}$: the data given in the question do not reproduce it.)
